before: A host could author a merge field only by building the five runs itself and landing them with insertFragment, which split and joined the paragraph and so was refused beside any locked control in it; rewriting a field's name took deleting it and inserting another, losing its formatting.
after: insertMergeField { paragraphId, offset, name, result, inside?, beside? } writes the field's five runs with the caret's run properties through the same landing an inline control uses; setMergeField { paragraphId, fieldNodeId, name, result } rewrites the instruction and the cached result in place. The engine owns the instruction's spelling; the name is the host's.
reason: Both ops reduce to canonical tree primitives the journal already replicates (a run split, a children insertion, node replacements of an instruction and of result runs). Released participants receive the resulting shared state, never the new op kinds.
